Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D decreased linearly from controls to at-risk individuals to those with full-threshold MDD.
Sentence: "A linear increase of inflammatory markers (CRP P=0.026; IL-6 P=0.090), cortisol (P=0.025) and decrease of vitamin D (P<0.001) was found across the entire sample (for example, from controls to those at risk and those with full-threshold MDD)."
Measured as: MDD status across controls, at-risk and full-threshold MDD (vitamin D as marker)
Population: 230 controls and 2333 participants at risk for or with MDD, aged 18-65 (NESDA)
Intervention: Measured vitamin D level (observational)
Comparator: Controls versus at-risk versus full-threshold MDD
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 2,563
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
